routing_policy.confidence_policy: Model self-reported confidence and retrieval scores are not calibrated probabilities of correctness. Tune abstention and routing on adjudicated development cases; report results on separate holdout cases.
routing_policy.primary_category_policy: Use the first explicit actionable concern in ticket order as primary; retain every distinct secondary category. If no actionable concern can be identified, use unknown. Original CSV category is provenance, not routing truth.

sections.heading: 3. Building a Basic RAG Pipeline (Knowledge Pipeline)

categories.scope: Dify app/dataset API access, key creation, key scope, authorization errors, rotation, and app API usage caps. Provider credential configuration belongs to model_providers.
contextual_signals: The requested key is for calling a published app or Knowledge API
Authentication succeeds against one object and fails against another
A monthly cap question concerns app API calls rather than model message credits

contrastive_examples.text: I published a chatbot and want to call it from my backend. Where is its API key?
My chatbot key returns 401 when uploading via the dataset API.
How do I connect my own OpenAI API key instead of built-in credits?
Does the free plan cap monthly API calls?

exclusions: OpenAI, Azure, Anthropic or other provider credentials used to run a model
Model response credits when the concern is not app API call quotas

categories.scope: Workspace ownership, roles, member invitation and access. SSO/audit/compliance requests are recognizable topics but require scope checks and specialist escalation for undocumented configuration.
contextual_signals: The object is a member, role or workspace access
Enterprise capabilities are asked about without configuration coverage in the guide

contrastive_examples.text: How do I invite a teammate on Professional?
Where do I configure SAML login?

exclusions: Published app or dataset API authentication
Enterprise SSO/SAML setup, audit export formats or certification guarantees as answerable instructions

categories.scope: Connecting model credentials/plugins, selecting app models, hosted credits versus provider billing and variable model credit usage. Custom model details require evidence or clarification.
contextual_signals: The requested key configures the model provider rather than authenticating a Dify app endpoint
The concern compares Dify-hosted model credits with direct provider usage
Credit consumption varies by selected model

contrastive_examples.text: Use our existing Azure OpenAI deployment with Dify.
Call my published Dify chatbot from a backend with an API key.
I connected Anthropic, and retrieval also returns zero chunks.

exclusions: Treating provider connection timing as proof of a retrieval-propagation delay
Enumerating custom runtime support absent from approved evidence

categories.scope: Knowledge ingestion, chunking, indexing, edits, hit testing, retrieval settings, missing chunks and upload troubleshooting; quota conditions also require billing evidence.
contextual_signals: The concern is retrieval or ingestion behavior rather than endpoint authorization
Reported upload errors are not yet a confirmed quota diagnosis
Document availability depends on completed indexing

contrastive_examples.text: Retrieval returns zero chunks for queries that used to work.
Uploading through the dataset API returns 401 with my app key.
Upload fails and I want to reduce Team seats to save money mid-cycle.

exclusions: 401 caused by key type mismatch is primarily API access
Self-hosted deployment, custom plugin SDK or workflow features beyond documented retrieval settings
Confirming account-specific upload causes without error and usage evidence

categories.scope: Workspace plan prices, quotas, credits renewal, payment methods, upgrades and downgrade effects. Mid-cycle proration and actual account state are not documented.
contextual_signals: The concern is a plan entitlement, payment policy or subscription change
Credit exhaustion alone does not identify a customer's plan or usage
Team billing is per workspace in the fictional guide

contrastive_examples.text: How much does Team cost and what limits does it include?
Why did model credit burn increase this week?

exclusions: Confirming an actual charge, credit balance or cap breach without account telemetry
Promising proration, Enterprise unlimited quotas, or undocumented feature entitlements
Replacing fictional fixture prices/policies with current website facts

categories.scope: No supported topic can be determined, conflicting context cannot identify the object/intent, or the request is outside the corpus. This is a routing fallback, not a mandatory escalation disposition.
contextual_signals: No identifiable product operation or concern
API key without enough context to determine app, dataset or provider
exclusions: Do not use unknown just because a known topic needs clarification or has undocumented configuration

concerns: Team entitlement and SSO for 40 members
multi_topic_examples.required_boundary: Conditional quota explanation; SSO configuration/entitlement needs scope checks; no confirmed account diagnosis.

concerns: reduce seats mid-cycle without losing data
multi_topic_examples.required_boundary: Ask for upload error; workspace billing does not establish per-seat savings; undocumented proration routes for review.
Do not infer causal propagation delay from temporal co-occurrence.
API call quotas are distinct from model message credits.

transport_supplement_policy.scope: Separately approved official Dify HTTP authorization transport evidence only. It must not override fictional key UI labels, scope, prices or plan policies.
